original_question: Which extremely rare genetic disorder, reported in only two siblings born to consanguineous Arab parents, is often associated with clubfoot?

final_qi.question: Which extremely rare genetic disorder, reported in only two siblings born to consanguineous Arab parents, is often associated with clubfoot?
final_qi.search_keyword: rare genetic disorder clubfoot consanguineous Arab parents
final_qi.short_answer: split-hand/foot malformation with long bone deficiency (SHFLD1)
final_qi.long_answer: The disorder is an extremely rare autosomal recessive condition that has been observed only in two siblings born to consanguineous Arab parents. It is known as split-hand/foot malformation with long bone deficiency (SHFLD1). This disorder is characterized by congenital limb malformations that include abnormalities of the hands and feet, with clubfoot being one of its associated manifestations. The condition maps to a specific region on chromosome 1q42.2-q43 and highlights the increased risk of rare congenital anomalies in populations with a high prevalence of consanguineous marriages.
